_comment: LULC and index thresholds calibrated for THIS dataset. Loaded at runtime by geospatial.lulc.load_calibration(); any key omitted falls back to the engine default.
dataset: real_rs_001 - Ralegaon Siddhi AOI, Parner taluka, Ahmednagar district, Maharashtra
notes: NDBI is NOT a built-up discriminator over dry basaltic terrain: measured NDBI spans +0.013 (p1) to +0.236 (p99) with a median of +0.136, so the textbook 'NDBI > 0.02 = built-up' rule labels 470 ha (65%) of this rural AOI as settlement. The built-up class is therefore taken from the > 0.20 tail (7.8 ha, ~1%), which is consistent with a village settlement plus hardpan.

Separating bare soil from built-up reliably requires a reference settlement layer (e.g. GHSL or a digitised revenue map) or a supervised classifier; with VNIR+SWIR alone the two are spectrally confusable. Treat 'built-up' here as provisional.

No open water is detectable in either pre-monsoon epoch: SWIR never falls below 0.1237 and MNDWI peaks at -0.058, i.e. there is genuinely no surface storage in this 726 ha window in May. A small water body (~0.16 ha by NDWI > 0.10, ~0.06 ha by MNDWI > 0) does appear post-monsoon. The zero is a real observation, not a detection failure.

NDVI thresholds transfer well: pre-monsoon p50 = 0.137 (fallow/scrub) and post-monsoon p50 = 0.482 (cropland) sit on either side of the 0.30 cropland cut, and the 0.50 dense-canopy cut captures the irrigated/riparian tail.
